# WebCodex v0.5.5

## Windows full-installer payload consistency

The Windows full installer is built around the same native Desktop NSIS package used to collect its source manifest. Reusing that exact package keeps the installed Desktop and Runtime bytes tied to the four program hashes in the published manifest, without a second Desktop compilation under another bundle configuration.

The existing Windows Environment path, installation ownership, private-state preservation, and recovery checks remain required. Program hash verification remains strict for Desktop and all three Runtime programs.

## Desktop setup and status

- Windows Codex setup discovers standard npm installations and the default standalone installation, with distinct guidance for a missing CLI, unavailable Node.js, and an unsupported or incomplete launcher. Codex CLI must still be installed separately and uses your existing Codex login or API configuration; models and account access are not bundled.
- SSH connections retain their latest verification time and result and provide an explicit action to verify again. Existing connections without saved verification history need one new verification.
- Local component status distinguishes an unavailable update candidate from a component that has not been checked, and reports the observed state of the Runtime owned by Desktop.

## Acceptance required before stable publication

Stable publication requires successful exact-source CI and native evidence, a successful formal release build, and verification of the frozen public prerelease assets. Native Windows x64 and ARM64 must each pass fresh installation, upgrade from an unconfigured upstream v0.5.0 Desktop, and upgrade from a configured upstream v0.5.0 Desktop with its owned Runtime running.

Those checks must verify the actual full installer, all four installed program hashes, source identity, preserved installation and Environment state, unrelated process survival, service restart, and owned cleanup. Both same-attempt reports must be retained and verified before the same Release can become stable/latest. Image publication and the Intel macOS Desktop DMG/checksum pair remain required final checks.

These are the release requirements; this note does not assert that any pending build, installation scenario, or publication has already succeeded. The existing v0.5.4 prerelease and its artifacts remain unchanged.
